Article (plain text of the PDF):

Rational Linear Relations and Laplace Equations for Dihedral
Modular Graph Functions up to Weight 11
Noah Schittenhelm
Hack-Nation 2026, Team Ninja Turtles

Preprint, October 4, 2026

Abstract
We study rational linear relations among two-loop dihedral modular graph functions
C(a, b, c) of weight w = a + b + c, together with E(w) and ζ(w). For the full dihedral
basis at weights 3, 5, 7 and 9 the relation space is numerically of dimension exactly one
per weight. At weight 9 it is spanned by 960E(9) + ζ(9) − 2160C(4, 4, 1) − 4320C(4, 3, 2) −
960C(3, 3, 3) = 0. At weight 11 the relation space was determined only on the sub-basis
C(5, 5, 1), C(5, 4, 2), C(5, 3, 3), C(4, 4, 3), E(11), ζ(11), where it is again one-dimensional. For
the full ten-function weight-11 basis the question is undecided. A counting of linearly
independent modular graph forms was given in [1], and the weight-9 result may be implied
there. We also verify inhomogeneous Laplace equations for C(3, 1, 1), C(2, 1, 1) and C(2, 2, 1).
The method is PSLQ on values at random points, followed by an exact leading-Laurentcoefficient check and independent evaluation. All modular-graph-function statements are
numerical observations at 4 verifier points, not theorems.
Keywords: modular graph functions, Eisenstein series, string theory one-loop amplitude,
Laplace equation, linear relations, low-energy expansion

1

Introduction

Modular graph functions appear as coefficients in the low-energy expansion of the one-loop
closed-string amplitude. They satisfy Laplace eigenvalue equations with inhomogeneous terms
that are polynomial in non-holomorphic Eisenstein series [2]. Relations of low weight have been
proved by an explicit map between graph forms [3], and all dihedral identities at weight seven
are in the literature [4]. Systematic basis decompositions of two- and three-point graph forms
are available [5]. A counting of linearly independent modular graph forms gives predictions for
higher, hitherto unexplored weights [1].
Open question: how many independent rational linear relations exist among all C(a, b, c)
of weight w, E(w) and ζ(w) for weights 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11, and which Laplace equations do the
functions satisfy?
Contribution: we determine the relation space numerically on the full dihedral basis at
weights 3, 5, 7 and 9. At weight 11 we determine it only on a six-function sub-basis. We verify
Laplace equations for three functions, and we reproduce holomorphic identities with Sturm-bound
certificates.
Summary of results.
• The weight-by-weight observations show that the relation space has dimension exactly one
on the full dihedral basis at weights 3, 5, 7 and 9, with the novelty statuses quoted there.
• A further observation gives the explicit weight-9 relation.
• The weight-11 observation gives the relation and its one-dimensional relation space on the
sub-basis only. The full ten-function weight-11 basis is undecided.
1

 • The Laplace observations give equations for C(3, 1, 1), C(2, 1, 1) and C(2, 2, 1).
• The propositions on holomorphic identities certify string-partition-function identities, and
a further proposition gives the eta-quotient span table.

Method

Relations. Candidate rational relations are obtained by PSLQ on function values at random
points. The failed weight-11 attempt on the full basis, at the points examined (6-8 points, up to
64 digits), found no relation. Each candidate is then checked in two ways:
• exact rational arithmetic on the leading Laurent coefficient;
• evaluation at the verifier’s own points, with relative residual below 1e-24.
Completeness. Completeness of a relation space is judged by a singular-value gap of the
normalised value matrix at an independent seed, 4712.
Laplace equations. They are checked at the 4 verifier points at 32 digits, with relative
residual at most 1e-14, using a finite-difference Laplacian, together with an exact leadingcoefficient check.
Holomorphic identities. A Sturm-bound certificate is used. For the identity of, the terms
lie in M2! (Γ0 (4)) and the coefficients q 0 ..q 11 vanish exactly, which exceeds the Sturm bound 1.
Trusted base and status. The trusted base is exact rational arithmetic for leading
coefficients and Sturm certificates, plus the verifier’s 32-digit evaluation of modular graph
functions. Everything about modular graph functions beyond the exact leading coefficient is a
numerical observation at the 4 verifier points, never a theorem. The weight-11 sub-basis came
from a human-guided exploration and was then verified by the code verifier. Everything is re-run
with the command in the Declarations.
The work was carried out by an automated, verifier-gated laboratory in which every statement
reported here was accepted only after an independent code check; its organisation is described in
Appendix A.

6

Discussion, limitations and open questions

The relation space has dimension exactly one at weights 3, 5, 7 and 9 on the full dihedral
basis. Each relation has the form (combination of C) = (rational) E(w)+ (rational) ζ(w). The
weight-11 relation has the same shape on a six-function sub-basis. All statements on modular
graph functions are numerical observations at 4 verifier points, with an exact check only of the
leading Laurent coefficient.
Open questions:
(i) What is the relation-space dimension for the full ten-function weight-11 basis? Higher
precision or a different method is needed.
(ii) What is the dimension at weight 6, where the gap criterion was not met?
(iii) Is the weight-9 result implied by the counting of [1] (status: inconclusive)?
(iv) Can the numerical relations be turned into proofs, as done for low weight in [3] [4]?

A

Agentic laboratory

The laboratory ran 8 rounds with 24 verified statements and 3 negative results. Every round was
preregistered before the experiment (prereg.md). Several agents with distinct roles proposed
candidates (for example numerical, skeptical and theoretical roles, as listed in the failed attempts).
Only statements accepted by the code verifier were kept. Counter-checks (adversarial tests)
numbered 30 in total: 2 passed, 27 did not pass, and 1 was not executable. “Did not pass” means
the false variant was rejected, which is the intended outcome. The two that passed did not
contradict the statements.

C

Verifier self-test

The verifier is tested with deliberately false variants, which it must reject. Examples:
• factor 1727 instead of 1728 in the discriminant identity, and 1729 instead of 1728;
• q 1 -coefficient 481 instead of 480 for θD16 ;
• ζ(5) coefficient 1/5 instead of 1/10, which gives residual 1.04e-01;
• ζ(9) coefficient 2 instead of 1;
• a sign flip of the ζ(11) term, which gives residual 5.71e-01.
All of these were rejected, so the verifier distinguishes exact leading coefficients and tight
residuals from near-misses.
